reviewer: AI (Claude) independent reviewers (blind solve + informed review), separate from the author; not a native-speaker or teacher review

qs.q: What is the writer's main point?
o: Tablets are harmful and should be removed from every classroom immediately.
Typing is too slow to be useful for students who take notes in class.
Handwriting aids learning, so schools should combine it with typing.
Teachers should stop asking students to edit and correct their drafts.
qs.why: 필자는 손글씨의 학습 효과를 말하며 두 방법을 함께 쓰자고 제안해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why does writing by hand help memory?
o: Pens make students feel calmer during long lectures.
Students must pick key ideas and put them in their own words.
Students can copy the lecture word for word and read it later.
Notebooks are lighter and easier to carry around than tablets.
qs.why: 손으로 쓰면 모든 말을 받아 적을 수 없어 중요한 것을 골라 자기 말로 바꾸게 돼요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that typing is faster?
o: To prove that handwriting is actually the quicker method
To admit a point in favor of the opposing view
To explain why tablets are cheaper for most schools
To show that teachers dislike the use of notebooks
qs.why: 반대 입장의 장점을 인정한 뒤 However로 자신의 주장을 이어 가요.

qs.q: The word “obsolete” in the first sentence is closest in meaning to
o: outdated
fragile
valuable
illegal
qs.why: obsolete는 ‘더 이상 쓰이지 않는, 구식의’라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply about a student who types a whole lecture?
o: The student will always earn lower scores than classmates.
The student probably cannot read his own handwriting.
The student is likely to finish editing sooner than others.
The student may not have thought deeply about the content.
qs.why: ‘완벽한 기록이지만 이해는 적을 수 있다’는 말에서 내용을 깊이 처리하지 않았음을 추론할 수 있어요.

patches.why: Replace unreliable line reference with sentence reference (q4 stem only).

qs.q: What is the writer's position on the issue?
o: The writer fully supports a complete ban on phones throughout the school day.
The writer suggests a compromise that considers both sides.
The writer believes teachers should watch every table.
The writer thinks lunch should be shorter for everyone.
qs.why: 양쪽 입장을 소개한 뒤 일부 구역만 휴대폰 금지로 하는 절충안을 제안해요.

qs.q: Which argument do supporters of phone use give?
o: Phones are useful for taking notes during lunch.
Screens make it easier for students to talk to friends.
A ban would save the school money on equipment.
Lunchtime is free time, and phones help students relax.
qs.why: 점심시간은 자유 시간이고 휴대폰이 긴장을 풀어 준다는 것이 찬성 측 논거예요.

qs.q: What does “This” refer to in “This would respect the freedom of those who want to relax with their devices”?
o: Banning phones from the whole lunchroom
Explaining the new rule to all students
Setting aside some tables as phone-free zones
Letting everyone use phones at every table
qs.why: This는 바로 앞 문장의 절충안, 즉 일부 테이블을 휴대폰 금지 구역으로 정하는 것을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does the phrase “a shared meal” suggest about the opponents' view?
o: Meals are best eaten quickly and alone.
Lunch should be a time for people to interact.
Food should be served by the students themselves.
Everyone should eat the same dishes at lunch.
qs.why: 함께 먹는 식사의 목적은 대화와 교류라는 의미를 담고 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say the rule should be explained clearly?
o: So that students understand the reasons instead of just obeying
So that teachers have much less work to do during the long lunch break
So that parents can send messages during lunch
So that students stop using phones at home
qs.why: 학생들이 이유를 이해하고 규칙을 받아들이게 하기 위해서예요.

qs.q: Why does less rainwater rush into the drains during storms?
o: Plants release water vapor into the drains.
Roofs of concrete and tar hold rain for a long time.
The soil of a green roof absorbs part of the water.
Building owners cover the drains in heavy weather.
qs.why: 흙이 빗물을 흡수해 배수구로 흘러드는 양이 줄어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the layer of plants “acts like a blanket” means that it
o: makes the building look soft and warm
covers the building to protect it from rain
hides ugly surfaces from people on the street
keeps the temperature inside more stable
qs.why: 담요처럼 겨울에는 따뜻하게, 여름에는 시원하게 해 주는 단열 효과를 비유한 거예요.

qs.q: Which word signals a change from advantages to disadvantages?
o: In addition
Still
Also
As
qs.why: Still은 앞의 장점과 대조되는 단점을 소개할 때 써요.

qs.q: Why do many experts recommend green roofs for new buildings?
o: Old buildings do not have any roofs at all.
New buildings need fewer plants than old ones do, so they cost less.
New buildings can be designed to carry the extra weight.
Green roofs are cheaper to remove from new buildings.
qs.why: 녹화 지붕은 무거워서 건물이 이를 지탱하도록 설계되어야 하기 때문이에요.
